title: Cookie, butter or sugar, with icing or non‑chocolate filling

content.title: About
content.content: This is a cookie made from a butter‑ or sugar‑based dough, topped with icing or filled with a non‑chocolate filling. Common icings are vanilla, fruit or caramel, while fillings may include jam, cream, nuts or marmalade.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tradition of icing cookies began in Europe in the 19th century.
In the United States, “Sugar Cookies” with a sweet glaze are a popular holiday treat, often decorated with colored sprinkles.
Fruit fillings such as strawberry or lemon jam are frequently used in festive assortments.
A glaze made from powdered sugar and egg white hardens quickly, creating a crisp surface.
In some regions these are called “shortbread” because of their crumbly texture.

items.title: Quick source of energy
items.content: Sugar and fats in the dough provide rapid glucose and energy for the body.

items.title: Contains small amounts of B‑vitamins
items.content: Flour and eggs supply thiamine (B1), riboflavin (B2) and niacin.

items.title: Calcium from dairy ingredients
items.content: When milk or butter is used, the cookie contributes a modest amount of calcium.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Gluten and dairy allergies
items.content: Traditional recipes contain wheat flour and dairy, which may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Possible trans‑fat content
items.content: Using margarine instead of butter can introduce trans fats, which are detrimental to heart health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cookies are convenient as a standalone snack, served with tea, or used in dessert platters. They can be further decorated with sprinkles, nuts or dried fruit.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature, away from direct sunlight. For longer storage, refrigerate to prevent the icing from softening.
